nodes.author: serenasundar
nodes.text:
Reiterating that Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) is not a new virus and there was no cause for alarm, the Clinical Infectious Diseases Society has stated that advancements in diagnostic technologies have improved the detection of HMPV in recent years.
https://t.co/zgmSj5lGck

nodes.author: serenasundar
nodes.text: The apparent increase in reported cases is likely due to heightened surveillance and better diagnostics rather than an actual rise in infections. HMPV was first identified in 2001 in the Netherlands, and is closely related to Respiratory Syncytial Virus.

nodes.author: serenasundar
nodes.text: It is a well-recognised cause of respiratory infections, particularly in children and the elderly. It accounts for approximately two to eight per cent of community respiratory viral infections globally.
